Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: Allows the comparability of underlying financial performance by excluding the impacts of exceptional items and is also the basis on which our dividend payout ratio policy is applied.
Calculation methodology: Profit after taxation attributable to BHP shareholders excluding any exceptional items attributable to BHP shareholders.

Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: On a per share basis, allows the comparability of underlying financial performance by excluding the impacts of exceptional items.
Calculation methodology: Underlying attributable profit divided by the weighted basic average number of shares.

Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: Used to help assess current operational profitability excluding the impacts of sunk costs (i.e. depreciation from initial investment). Each is a measure that management uses internally to assess the performance of the Group’s segments and make decisions on the allocation of resources.
Calculation methodology: Earnings before net finance costs, depreciation, amortisation and impairments, taxation expense, discontinued operations and exceptional items. Underlying EBITDA includes BHP’s share of profit/(loss) from investments accounted for using the equity method including net finance costs, depreciation, amortisation and impairments and taxation expense/(benefit).

Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: Underlying EBITDA excluding third-party product EBITDA, divided by revenue excluding third-party product revenue.

Used to help assess current operational profitability excluding net finance costs and taxation expense (each of which are managed at the Group level) as well as discontinued operations and any exceptional items.
Calculation methodology: Earnings before net finance costs, taxation expense, discontinued operations and any exceptional items. Underlying EBIT includes BHP’s share of profit/(loss) from investments accounted for using the equity method including net finance costs and taxation expense/(benefit).

Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: Earnings before net finance costs, taxation expense and discontinued operations. Profit from operations includes Revenue, Other income, Expenses excluding net finance costs and BHP’s share of profit/(loss) from investments accounted for using the equity method including net finance costs and taxation expense/(benefit).
Used as part of our Capital Allocation Framework to assess efficient deployment of capital. Represents the total outflows of our operational investing expenditure.
Calculation methodology: Purchases of property, plant and equipment and exploration expenditure.

Reasons why we believe the APMs are usef: It is a key measure used as part of our Capital Allocation Framework. Reflects our operational cash performance inclusive of investment expenditure, which helps to highlight how much cash was generated in the period to be available for the servicing of debt and distribution to shareholders.
Calculation methodology: Net operating cash flows less net investing cash flows.
